s1.syndrome_frame: Painful skin lesion on the chest with a 2-week history
salient_findings: Large, crusted, erythematous plaque on the right chest
Patient is taking prednisone, 10 mg, daily
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 50s
2-week history of a painful area on the right lateral chest
Taking prednisone, 10 mg, daily
Previous treatments included methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, glycopyrrolate, oral antibiotics, topical corticosteroids, topical calcineurin inhibitors, and topical antibiotics
Biopsy was previously performed
Laboratory values within normal limits for intact parathyroid hormone, ionized calcium, and phosphorus

shortlist.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of painful skin lesions and previous treatments have been unsuccessful, which is consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a large, crusted, erythematous plaque on the right chest, which could be a manifestation of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of a painful area on the right lateral chest, which could be a sign of squamous cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Eczema herpeticum
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of taking prednisone, which could increase the risk of eczema herpeticum

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a large, crusted, erythematous plaque on the right chest, which could be a manifestation of basal cell carcinoma

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a large, crusted, erythematous plaque, along with a history of unsuccessful treatments and the presence of a painful area, is most consistent with Pyoderma gangrenosum, a condition characterized by ulcerative skin lesions that are often painful and can be refractory to treatment.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: While possible, the lack of specific biopsy results detailing lymphoma and the clinical presentation does not strongly suggest this diagnosis over Pyoderma gangrenosum.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The description of the lesion as a crusted, erythematous plaque does not typically align with the usual presentation of squamous cell carcinoma, which often appears as a firm, rough-surfaced lesion.

rejected.label: Eczema herpeticum
rejected.why: Eczema herpeticum is characterized by disseminated herpes simplex infection in the setting of eczema, which is not indicated in the patient's history or clinical presentation.

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Basal cell carcinoma typically presents as a slow-growing, painless lesion, which does not match the patient's painful, rapidly evolving condition.
